chapter_title: Concerning the Three Creations of the Flesh: the o

spiritual_reading.full_translation:
Every affection that appears in the outer human, and every other formed quality in the ultimate degree, is fixed and made stable through the complete ordering of the three degrees of life. Some are brought forth from disordered beginnings that do not rightly receive influx, so that what comes to birth is a distorted determination. Others, however, take form by a more direct reception of their ruling love, and thus come into their own quality according to their kind.

Their sustenance is likewise threefold: they can be fed by inward wisdom, if they are willing to receive it; but if they are unwilling, they take in only truths that remain merely in potency and works that are pleasant outwardly. They appropriate these into themselves, and by that appropriation they express, in their own way, the three universal patterns of life from their inborn quality, and they abide in those patterns so long as they remain in the outer state. While they are immersed there, their ruling cravings seize them and carry them. The governing influx present in ultimates gathers all operative abilities under its disposal and arranges them for use.

Then, in the first ordering of the outer degree, the initial emergence of good and truth was set forth in a general and undistinguished way. From a contrary intention there arose harmful and bitter perceptions, together with stubborn persuasions, prickly defenses of selfhood, and other like falsities and evils in the outermost mind.

For such an intention belongs to dominions that delight in destroying what is innocent and living. Yet the milder and merely natural delights that were set in place belong to rudimentary and common things of the external life, because such delights are what they are in their own character. Nevertheless, that destructive intention, so far as it first shows itself in outwardly pleasant works and in rudimentary truth, and has not yet descended into the full profanation of will and understanding, also brings forth perceptions that yield works able to serve as nourishment, because those delights are then softened in externals.

But again, that destructive intention, when it flows from powers that both harm innocence and at the same time cling to outward forms of truth and to mild natural pleasures, produces perceptions that yield no nourishment. The works that proceed from them incline neither toward living good nor toward confirmed evil, and thus remain without a determinate spiritual life.

paragraph_translations.translation: Every affection that appears in the outer human, and likewise every other formed quality in the ultimate degree, is confirmed and established through the full ordering of the three degrees of life. Some are brought forth from disordered beginnings that lack a proper reception of influx, so that what results is a distorted formation. Others, however, shape themselves by a more direct reception of their ruling love and so come into a determinate quality according to their own kind.
paragraph_translations.connection: OPENS the chapter by stating how outer qualities are established through the three degrees and how they arise in orderly or disorderly ways.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source wording is corrupt (“three archetypes abortions… miscarriages”); rendered as orderly vs disordered formation from reception of influx.

paragraph_translations.translation: Their sustenance is likewise according to the three degrees: they can be fed by wisdom within, if they are willing to receive it; otherwise they take in only such interior truths as lie merely in potency, and such works as are outwardly pleasing but not inwardly understood. They appropriate these things into themselves, and by that appropriation they express, in their own way, the three universal patterns of life from their inborn quality, and they remain within those patterns during their state in the outer degree. When they are immersed there, they are taken hold of by their own ruling impulses and carried as those impulses determine. The directing influx that is sent forth into ultimates gathers the operative abilities under its command and disposes them for action.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by explaining threefold spiritual nourishment, appropriation, and government in ultimates.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Ambassador” and bracketed fragments are unclear; taken as a governing influx in ultimates ordering powers for action.

paragraph_translations.translation: Then, in the first ordering of these outer things, the initial growth of truth and good in the natural degree was set forth in a general and common way. From a contrary influx, there were formed bitter and harmful perceptions, together with stubborn persuasions, prickly defenses of selfhood, and other like falsities and evils that arise in the outmost mind.
paragraph_translations.connection: SHIFTS from nourishment to the first ordering of externals and the arising of contrary forms.
paragraph_translations.notes: List of growths is translated as kinds of falsity/evil in externals; exact mapping of each item is approximate but consistent with their harmful function.

paragraph_translations.translation: For that intention belongs to dominions that delight in destroying what is innocent and living. Yet the more harmless and merely natural delights that were set in place belong to the rudimentary and common things of the outer life, because such delights are what they are in their essence. Nevertheless, the intention that descended from those dominions, insofar as it first presents itself in outwardly pleasing works and in rudimentary truth and not yet in the full profanation of the will and understanding, also produces perceptions that yield works which can serve as nourishment, because those delights are then softened and made pleasant in externals.
paragraph_translations.connection: DEVELOPS by distinguishing destructive intention from milder external delights and showing how even corrupted intention can yield outwardly useful works at first.
paragraph_translations.notes: The source contrasts what is “from flesh-eating rulers” with what is “grass and gourds,” and then says it is not yet in “flesh and blood”; rendered as degrees of corruption/profanation vs milder external states.

paragraph_translations.translation: But again, the intention that descended from powers that destroy innocence and yet also cling to outward forms of truth and to mild natural delights, produces perceptions that yield no spiritual nourishment. The works that proceed from them incline neither to genuine good nor to confirmed evil, and thus remain without a living quality.
paragraph_translations.connection: CONCLUDES by describing a mixed intention that yields works devoid of spiritual vitality.
paragraph_translations.notes: “Fruits belong neither to good nor evil” is taken as works that are spiritually indifferent/undetermined; the precise identity of the “powers” is not further specified in the source.

spiritual_reading.overall_coherence: Coherent as a single teaching: it moves from the establishment of outer affections through three degrees, to their nourishment, then to the first ordering of externals and the emergence of harmful perceptions, and finally to distinctions among intentions that produce nourishing, harmful, or spiritually inert works. The main stumbles come from textual corruption (“abortions/miscarriages,” “Ambassador”), but the through-line of three-degree influx, appropriation, and resultant quality remains consistent.

findings.diagnosis: Genuine difficulty from damaged/garbled Vorlage rather than a voice-insertion. The paragraph is supposed to introduce a threefold taxonomy of earthly/animal formation, but key terms are corrupt (“three archetypes… abortions… miscarriages”), forcing the spiritual reading to paraphrase into an abstract influx/doctrine. The narrative function (set up: three likenesses; then two subtypes) is still visible, so removing anything would not restore clarity.
findings.evidence: Text: “confirm them in three likeness[es]: some from [three archetypes] abortions. Others, however, form their own selves in their shape [miscarriages].” The spiritual notes: “source wording is corrupt (‘three archetypes abortions… miscarriages’).” The reader did not stumble because of an administrative overlay (no ranks/jurisdictions), but because the technical nouns are broken; yet the skeleton ‘three… some… others…’ is coherent as correspondential classification.

findings.diagnosis: Insertion into a functional (correspondential) discussion: a brief administrative/jurisdictional tag has been dropped into an otherwise correspondential account of threefold nourishment. The paragraph reads smoothly as a functional teaching until an abrupt, fragmentary authority statement with “Ambassador” and “powers of Light… established over,” which does not participate in the ‘nourishment/appropriation/lusts’ story and is syntactically discontinuous.
findings.evidence: Text’s functional run: “their nourishment is thre[e]… they eat seeds and fruit… they swallow the three archetyp[es]… remain… seized… by the lusts.” Then the seam: “The Ambassador [members] all powers [of Light is established over].” The spiritual reading notes the stumble explicitly: “‘Ambassador’ and bracketed fragments are unclear; taken as a governing influx in ultimates ordering powers for action.” That is exactly the kind of forced harmonization expected when an administrative control-phrase intrudes into a correspondential process-description.
findings.scope: Remove the intrusive tag at the end of ¶3: “The Ambassador [members] all powers [of Light is established over].”

findings.diagnosis: Clean correspondential substrate: planting/growth imagery is taught by function (what plants are like/produce), and the list of bitter trees/reeds/thorns/briers naturally supports a moral or qualitative mapping. No governance lists or jurisdictional named powers; the narrative transitions appropriately from ‘nourishment’ to ‘first planting/order’ as a next stage of formation.
findings.evidence: Text: “first [the first planting]… Plant them generally… shoots and grass. It formed the bad, bitter trees, the reeds and the thorns…” The spiritual reading’s ‘Connection’ reports no narrative break: “SHIFTS… to the first ordering of externals,” and the notes admit only item-level mapping uncertainty, not structural mismatch. The teaching arises from what the growths do/are (bitter, thorny), not who rules them.

findings.diagnosis: Mostly correspondential (diet/plant-fruit typology) but with mild administrative coloring via ‘rulers/powers’ language. Here, however, the rulers are not presented as a ranked inventory or jurisdictional administration; they function as explanatory agents for why certain ‘thoughts’ produce certain fruits (nourishing, non-nourishing, indifferent). The spiritual reading’s ‘rulers’ interpretation is a smoothing of mythic diction, but the underlying logic still teaches by outcomes (what is produced) rather than by offices.
findings.evidence: Text: “thought belongs to the flesh-eating rulers… planted… grass and gourds… thought… formed the trees that shall give nourishing fru[it]… Again, this thought… from the powers… formed the trees that shall not produce any nourishment. Their fruits belong neither to good nor evil.” Even with “rulers/powers,” the paragraph’s structure is functional causation: kind of thought → kind of tree/fruit → nourishment-value. The spiritual reading did not flag a break here; it maintained the through-line about intentions producing nourishing/harmful/inert works.

textual_criticism.summary: 4 findings: (1) ¶2 is damaged but structurally coherent (no excision). (2) ¶3 contains a mixed-voice seam; an administrative/jurisdictional tag (“The Ambassador… powers of Light… established over”) disrupts the correspondential nourishment narrative → recommend excision of that tag. (3) ¶4 is clean correspondential planting imagery (no action). (4) ¶5–¶6 remain essentially correspondential despite mythic ‘rulers/powers’ diction (no action). Total: excise 1, annotate 0, none 3.
